newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil sees no Latin arms race after U.S. decision.
newsitem.headline: Brazil sees no Latin arms race after U.S. decision.

text.p: Brazilian Foreign Minister Luiz Felipe Lampreia said on Monday that the U.S. decision to allow sales of sophisticated weapons to Latin America was not likely to set off an arms race in the region.
U.S. President Bill Clinton last week ended a 20-year policy of not selling weapons such as high-performance fighter jets and other advanced weapons to Latin America.
The policy was adopted by the Carter administration at a time when most of Latin America was ruled by military regimes.
"Brazil views this issue with calm because conditions in Latin America are not likely to prompt an arms race," Lampreia told foreign journalists at a lunch in Rio de Janeiro.
He said Brazil had no plans at present to buy these type of weapons from the United States.
The change in U.S. policy will clear the way for U.S. defence contractors to compete in the sale of warplanes to Chile, which is planning to replace its ageing fighters.
Chile has shown interest in buying up to 24 F-16 jets made by Lockheed Martin.
